newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Wall Street rise boosts South African stocks S.African stocks...
newsitem.headline: Wall Street rise boosts South African stocks S.African stocks...

text.p: A bullish opening start from Wall Street gave South African stocks a late rush of blood to the head as they shook off a lethargic afternoon mood to roar upwards before the close of trade.

Fresh U.S. economic data released in New York quashed inflation fears and spurred the Dow to roar ahead with its industrial index topping 5,800 for the first time in history. South African shares rapidly followed them up.
"Wall Street gave things a real boost," said one dealer.

The all-share index closed up 55.8 points at 6,870.4 as industrials roared ahead 65.3 points to finish at 8,106. Dealers said the early dominance of futures-related trade was broken as blue-chip investors poured back in.

Golds have been jittery all week ahead of a key meeting later on Friday of the International Monetary Fund which is to discuss the possible sale of five million ounces of gold to help fund aid to developing countries.
But the gold index firmed as dealers were in an upbeat mood, saying that any decision to go-ahead with such a sale was already factored into the bullion price.
The gold index ended strongly, finishing up 22.2 points to 1,765.2. The gold futures contract was at 1,215/20 from 1,200.
